title: Prepared presentation, conormal charts and cleared relations for Popescu lifting
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let pi be an element of R, and let Cbar be a finitely presented R/pi^2R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], compatible with its R-algebra structure. There are finite natural numbers n,m,r, polynomials f_l,a_k,h_{klj},g_{kl} in P=R[x_1,...,x_n], subsets E_k of {1,...,m}, and a surjective presentation map epsilon:(R/pi^2R)[x_1,...,x_n] to Cbar whose kernel is the ideal Ibar generated by the reduced f_l. Set C0=(R/pi^2R)[x]/Ibar. The elements epsilon(abar_k) cover every prime at which Cbar is smooth over R/pi^2R [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. For each k, (C0)_{abar_k} is smooth over R/pi^2R; |E_k|<=n; the classes of the reduced f_j for j in E_k give a basis of the localized conormal module Ibar/Ibar^2 [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; and the differentials of (C0)_{abar_k} over R/pi^2R have a basis of cardinality n-|E_k|. In P one has a_k f_l=sum_{j in E_k} h_{klj}f_j+pi^2g_{kl} for all k,l. For l in E_k, h_{klj}=a_k delta_{lj} for every j and g_{kl}=0.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07CP, original DAG steps 1--4, preparation (1)--(4) (Tag 07CP; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP)

proof.text: (Presentation; Noetherianity.) Since $\bar C$ is of finite presentation over $R/\pi^2R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], choose a presentation $\bar C\cong(R/\pi^2R)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_m)$ and lifts $f_j\in P:=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of the $\bar f_j$. Put $\bar P=(R/\pi^2R)[x_1,\dots,x_n]=P/\pi^2P$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)\subseteq P$, $\bar I=(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_m)\subseteq\bar P$ its image, and for $E\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, $I_E=(f_j,\ j\in E)$ with image $\bar I_E\subseteq\bar P$. Thus $\bar C=\bar P/\bar I=P/(I+\pi^2P)$; we write $x_i$ also for the images of the variables, and $\bar a$ for the image in $\bar C$ of $a\in P$. $\bar C$ is a finitely generated algebra over the Noetherian ring $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}\bar C$ be the set of primes at which $R/\pi^2R\to\bar C$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1452-1460 ('We choose a presentation ... Since R is Noetherian, so is C-bar'); Stacks writes the presentation over R, we present over R/pi^2R and lift the equations, which is the same up to adding pi^2

proof.text: (Finitely many good elements: Stacks (1), (2).) For each $\bar{\mathfrak q}\in W$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-free-conormal-basis] to the ring $R/\pi^2R$, the presentation $\bar C=\bar P/\bar I$ and $\bar{\mathfrak q}$: there are $a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\in P$ (lift an element of $\bar P$) with $\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\notin\bar{\mathfrak q}$ and $V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$ such that $\bar C_{\bar a}$ is smooth over $R/\pi^2R$, $(\bar I/\bar I^2)_{\bar a}$ is free over $\bar C_{\bar a}$ on the classes of $\bar f_j$, $j\in V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, and $\Omega_{\bar C_{\bar a}/(R/\pi^2R)}$ is free of rank $n-|V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}|$ ($a=a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$). Let $T\subseteq\bar C$ be the set of all $\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$. The ideal $(T)$ is finitely generated ($\bar C$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]); each of finitely many generators is a combination of finitely many elements of $T$, so $(T)=(t_1,\dots,t_r)$ with $t_k\in T$. Choose for each $k$ one $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ with $t_k=\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ and put $a_k=a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, $E_k=V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$. Then: (1) $W=\bigcup_kD(\bar a_k)$: a prime $\bar{\mathfrak q}\in W$ does not contain $\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\in(T)$, so it misses some $t_k$; conversely $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ smooth gives $D(\bar a_k)\subseteq W$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]; (2) $(\bar I/\bar I^2)_{\bar a_k}$ is free over $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ on the classes of $\bar f_j$, $j\in E_k$; (2') $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ is smooth over $R/\pi^2R$ and $\Omega_{\bar C_{\bar a_k}/(R/\pi^2R)}$ is free of rank $n-|E_k|$. Properties (1), (2), (2') only depend on $D(\bar a_k)$ and the ring $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$; so they persist when $a_k$ is replaced by $a'_k\in P$ with $\bar a'_k=\bar a_k^{s}$ for some $s\ge1$ (then $\bar C_{\bar a'_k}=\bar C_{\bar a_k}$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1460-1474 (the smooth locus is quasi-compact, Topology 0052; Lemma 07C6 gives a_1..a_r with (1), (2)); the quasi-compactness is replaced by the equivalent finite generation of the ideal (T), and (2') is read off from the proof of 07C6

proof.text: (Nakayama: Stacks (3).) Fix $k$. In $\bar P_{a_k}$ let $J=\bar I\bar P_{a_k}$ and $M=(\bar I/\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}$, a finitely generated $\bar P_{a_k}$-module. By (2) the localization of $\bar I/\bar I^2$ at $a_k$ is generated by the classes of $\bar f_j$, $j\in E_k$, i.e. $\bar I_{a_k}=(\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}+(\bar I^2)_{a_k}$ (localization is exact [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]), hence $M=JM$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] there is $e\in\bar P_{a_k}$ with $e-1\in J$ and $eM=0$. Write $e-1=\bar b/a_k^N$ with $b\in I$ (lift the numerator from $\bar I$ to $I$), so $e=\overline{(a_k^N+b)}/a_k^N$. Replace $a_k$ by $a'_k=a_k(a_k^N+b)$: since $\bar b=0$ in $\bar C$, $\bar a'_k=\bar a_k^{N+1}$, so (1), (2), (2') persist (Step 2); and $(\bar I/\bar I_{E_k})_{a'_k}$ is a localization of $M$ in which the annihilator $a_k^Ne=\overline{a_k^N+b}$ of $M$ is a unit, so it is $0$. This gives (3): $(\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}=\bar I_{a_k}$ in $\bar P_{a_k}$. (Stacks says 'replacing $a_k$ by $a_kb_k$'; with $b_k\in I$ that element maps to $0$ in $\bar C$, so the intended replacement is $a_k(a_k^N+b_k)$, as here.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1475-1484 ('By (2) and Nakayama's lemma ... After replacing a_k by a_k b_k we get (3)')

proof.text: (Relations (4).) By (3), for every $k$ and $\ell$, $\bar f_\ell/1\in(\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}$, i.e. $\bar f_\ell/1=\sum_{j\in E_k}(\bar y_j/a_k^s)\bar f_j$ in $\bar P_{a_k}$; equality in $\bar P_{a_k}$ means equality in $\bar P$ after multiplying by a power of $a_k$, so $a_k^t\bar f_\ell=\sum_{j\in E_k}\bar h_j\bar f_j$ in $\bar P$ for some $t$ and $\bar h_j\in\bar P$; lifting to $P$, $a_k^tf_\ell-\sum_{j\in E_k}h_jf_j\in\pi^2P$. Taking one $t$ for all (finitely many) $k,\ell$ and replacing each $a_k$ by $a_k^t$ (allowed by Step 2; (3) persists as $\bar P_{a_k^t}=\bar P_{a_k}$) we obtain $h^j_{k,\ell},g_{k,\ell}\in P$ with (4) $a_kf_\ell=\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}f_j+\pi^2g_{k,\ell}$ for all $k\in\{1,\dots,r\}$, $\ell\in\{1,\dots,m\}$; for $\ell\in E_k$ we take instead $h^j_{k,\ell}=a_k\delta_{\ell j}$ and $g_{k,\ell}=0$, for which (4) holds trivially.

theorem exists_popescu_lift_preparation (R : Type a) (Cbar : Type c)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Cbar] [Algebra R Cbar] [IsNoetherianRing R] (π : R)
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    [IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    [FinitePresentation (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar] :
    ∃ d : PopescuLiftPresentation R Cbar π, d.Prepared
